title: Orientation
tagline: Set boundaries, align stakeholders, and baseline repository hygiene.

tasks.text: Draft the project charter stating target audience, core problem, and hard non-goals
tasks.doneWhen: Charter is documented in docs/charter.md and approved by engineering and product leads.

tasks.text: Initialize Git repository with standard branch protection rules and .gitignore
tasks.doneWhen: Main branch requires pull requests, status checks pass, and secret patterns are ignored.

tasks.text: Document runtime prerequisites, node/compiler engine pins, and package manager lockfile
tasks.doneWhen: engines field in package.json and .tool-versions or .nvmrc match team environment.

tasks.text: Define stakeholder contact roster and decision escalation pathways
tasks.doneWhen: RACI matrix or team README lists product owner, tech lead, and security reviewer.

tasks.text: Establish development environment setup guide and single-command local bootstrap
tasks.doneWhen: A new engineer can clone and successfully execute bootstrap script within 15 minutes.

existing.text: Audit existing git history, active branches, and stale unmerged pull requests
existing.doneWhen: Stale branches older than 60 days are cataloged and dead code branches archived.

existing.text: Run automated dependency vulnerability audit on inherited package manifests
existing.doneWhen: Critical and high CVE vulnerabilities are identified with documented mitigation plans.

existing.text: Map legacy codebase architecture, undocumented dependencies, and undocumented runtime services
existing.doneWhen: Architecture diagram reflects actual running components, cron jobs, and shared data stores.

existing.text: Verify local build and test execution from a fresh checkout without developer overrides
existing.doneWhen: Clean repository clone compiles and existing test suite executes with zero failures.

existing.text: Inventory third-party API keys, environment credentials, and production secret sprawl
existing.doneWhen: All credentials identified, moved to a secure vault, and removed from commit history.

existing.text: Check license compliance of inherited dependencies and proprietary dependencies
existing.doneWhen: Dependency license report generated and verified against organization legal policy.

existing.text: Benchmark baseline test coverage and identify critical untracked business paths
existing.doneWhen: Baseline coverage report generated and top three untested high-risk workflows documented.

existing.text: Document legacy technical debt backlog with severity rankings and migration impact
existing.doneWhen: Technical debt catalog created with estimated effort and priority in project tracker.

prompts.title: Project Kickoff & Charter Generator
prompts.expectedOutput: A structured markdown document ready for docs/charter.md with clear boundary definitions.

prompts.title: Existing Codebase Triage Prompt
prompts.template:
You are reviewing an existing legacy codebase for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" located at {{REPO_PATH}}.
Stack: {{STACK}}.
Users: {{USERS}}.

Analyze the codebase intake checklist and create a triage report detailing:
1. Recommended dependency modernization strategy
2. Secret scanning and credential rotation sequence
3. Critical regression test strategy before making any modifications
4. Phased technical debt remediation roadmap
prompts.expectedOutput: A 4-step triage and stabilization plan prioritizing business continuity and safety.

notes: Resist the temptation to start coding before writing down non-goals; scope creep is cheapest to kill during Orientation.
Always enforce branch protection rules immediately on repository creation. It prevents accidental pushes to main.

prompts.title: Customer Discovery Script & Question Generator

You are designing a customer discovery protocol for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}".
Target audience: {{USERS}}
Problem context: {{ONE_LINE}}

Generate a structured 30-minute user interview guide with:
1. Non-leading warmup questions to establish user context
2. Five open-ended questions exploring their existing workflow and painful friction points
3. Questions measuring current financial/time costs of manual workarounds
4. Red flags and false positives to watch for during responses
prompts.expectedOutput: A clean interview guide prioritizing Mom Test principles (no pitching, focus on past actions).

prompts.title: Competitive Differentiator Matrix
prompts.template:
Analyze the market landscape for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" serving {{USERS}}.
One-line summary: {{ONE_LINE}}
Tech stack: {{STACK}}

Identify the 3 closest alternative products or standard manual workflows.
Provide a comparison table detailing:
- Strengths and core target persona
- Friction points and user complaints
- Pricing/cost friction
- The "unfair advantage" or unique value proposition {{PROJECT_NAME}} must exploit
prompts.expectedOutput: A structured markdown comparison table and summary of defensible product moats.

notes: Never ask users "Would you use an app that does X?". Ask "Tell me about the last time you dealt with X and how you handled it."
If users currently solve the problem with spreadsheets or ad-hoc scripts, that is proof of demand—build on their mental model.

prompts.title: Gherkin User Story Specifier
prompts.template:
For "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" ({{ONE_LINE}}), target audience {{USERS}}:
Break down the primary user workflow into 3 detailed user stories.
For each story specify:
1. Title and Story statement: "As a [role], I want to [action], so that [outcome]"
2. Preconditions and edge cases
3. At least 3 scenarios formatted in strict Gherkin syntax:
   Scenario: [Happy path / Validation error / Failure recovery]
   Given [precondition]
   When [user action]
   Then [expected verifiable system response]
prompts.expectedOutput: Executable Gherkin scenarios ready for automated test specifications or engineering tickets.

prompts.title: Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) Generator
prompts.template:
Generate a Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) contract for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" built with {{STACK}}.
Users: {{USERS}}.
Target timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}.

Specify concrete numeric thresholds for:
1. Performance: P50, P95, and P99 API latency limits
2. Availability & Reliability: SLA/SLO percentages, MTBF, MTTR
3. Security & Compliance: Authentication rules, encryption in transit and at rest
4. Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 Level AA compliance checkpoints
5. Scalability: Initial capacity vs 10x surge expectations
prompts.expectedOutput: A formal NFR document table with metric, target threshold, measurement tool, and alert trigger.

notes: Ambiguity in requirements multiplies in cost by 10x in development and 100x in production. Clarify edge cases now.
Always specify error states and empty states in requirements; apps spend substantial user time in zero-data states.

prompts.title: Architecture Decision Record (ADR) Drafter

Draft a formal Architecture Decision Record (ADR) for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}".

System context: {{ONE_LINE}}

Structure the ADR following standard format:
1. Title: [e.g. ADR-001: Adoption of Client-side State vs Server State]
2. Status: Proposed / Accepted
3. Context: What technical and operational constraints drove this choice?

prompts.expectedOutput: A complete, production-ready markdown ADR formatted for the repository docs/adr/ folder.

prompts.title: Failure Mode & System Resilience Analyzer
prompts.template:
Analyze potential systemic failure modes for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" with stack {{STACK}}.

Map out failure scenarios for:
1. Database connectivity loss or sudden 10x read replica lag
2. External 3rd party API outage or 5-second latency spikes

4. Memory exhaustion under unexpected payload sizes
For each failure mode, prescribe the exact architectural defensive pattern to prevent cascading collapse.

prompts.title: Zero-Downtime Migration Guide
prompts.template:
For "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" running on {{STACK}}:
Explain how to execute a zero-downtime database migration for:
- Renaming a high-traffic column
- Adding a NOT NULL constraint with default value on a large table
- Splitting a table into two without taking the application offline
Provide the step-by-step expand-and-contract deployment sequence.
prompts.expectedOutput: A phased expand-contract migration playbook preventing table locks and downtime.

notes: Every foreign key should almost certainly have an index on the referencing table to prevent table scans on joins and deletes.
Never run schema migrations that drop or rename columns in the same release that changes the application code using them.

prompts.title: OWASP Threat Modeling & Attack Surface Reviewer
prompts.template:
Perform an OWASP Top 10 security audit for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}".
Tech stack: {{STACK}}
Description: {{ONE_LINE}}
Users: {{USERS}}

Analyze the attack surface across:
1. Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR): Can User A access User B's resource?
2. Injection vulnerabilities (SQL, NoSQL, command injection)
3. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) & Content Security Policy (CSP) directives
4. Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) & SameSite cookie attributes

Provide concrete remediation code snippets for each risk.

prompts.title: Strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) Generator
prompts.template:
Generate a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) and security headers configuration for "{{PROJECT_NAME}}" on {{STACK}}.
Directives needed:
- default-src, script-src, style-src, img-src, connect-src, frame-ancestors
- Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) with max-age=31536000 and includeSubDomains
- X-Frame-Options: DENY
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

prompts.title: Web Vitals & Bundle Optimization Plan

1. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): Font preloading, critical CSS, hero image compression
